utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed, Mr. Petrovic, that there was a preliminary matter to be raised by the Simatovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Very briefly, yesterday document D678 was admitted as a public exhibit. However, in keeping with the instructions you issued at the start of the testimony of the current witness, it should be admitted as an exhibit under seal. So I would apply for a change of status with regard to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since we are in open session, I'll not go into any further details. But the status of D678 is changed into a confidential exhibit. We'll have a further look at it. Then could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Draca.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Jordash will now continue his examination -- his cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Draca. Just picking up on one issue from yesterday: Dusan Orlovic. When did he leave the RSK, and where did he go? Are you able to confirm that he went to Belgrade and worked from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left the RSK sometime in December of 1991. He would occasionally come to Knin on private business, but I wouldn't see him on these occasions. He left for Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, as far as you were aware, did not continue acting within the state security within the RSK or conducting any professional business within the RSK of that nature.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the subject I want to now ask you about is the financing of the Krajina MUP and, included with that, the financing of the Krajina DB. Now, you told on the 31st of January that in 1991 as the conflict developed and the Krajina State Security Service was created, it was financed in the same way as the public security service at the early stage through donations. You recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, could I just inquire as to how you knew that to be the case?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel speak in the mike, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that because I was part of the system. I would see colleagues from both public and state security on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, there came a point in time when, as you told us, Martic disbanded the DB; November and early December of 1991. You, then, I think you told us yesterday, began working for the TO before then again working for the DB in August of 1992. In the period where you were working for the TO, were you able to view or did you have any information concerning the financing of the Krajina MUP immediately before the Vance Plan and as the Vance Plan was implemented?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period of time, I was practically on the border-line. I wouldn't go to Knin very often. I would go more oven to Benkovac. I think that the cash flow was established by that time and that the government budget financed the police force. But I can't recall exactly when it was that the government was set up and that the budget was basically executed for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's try to break this down a bit. First of all, do you agree with me that the way that the RSK authorities interpreted the Vance Plan was to effectively turn - and I'm generalising, but I'll come to specifics in a minute - but was to effectively turn the army into the police force?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. But with far fewer forces. Most of the RSK soldiers who had been mobilised at an earlier date went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So what that meant, effectively, was that it was the army which was responsible, as far as the RSK authorities was concerned, with setting up, supplying, financing the Krajina police, post-Vance?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the police had its own budget within the government, I suppose that your statement is true. But I can't tell you to what extent the army contributed towards the finances. At any rate, the police did have its own budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And let's get to specifics. And there's nothing you've said that I disagree with, I just want to see if you can help us with the specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have, please, on the screen 65 ter 5599, ERN 0668-2993-B/C/S and -ET, and the e-court page 31, the English, and 31 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is a notebook written by Mladic. I want to see if you can assist in relation to the details concerning his observations of the implementation of the Vance Plan. Let's go, if we can, straight to e-court page 41 of the English and 42 of the B/C/S. And the date we're looking at is the 20th of February, 1992. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, the page we saw just in a flash a minute ago seems to be the one corresponding with the page in B/C/S. So could we move to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is the one, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is the one. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And Babic [sic] writes: "There is an idea that some of our people be positioned in the government and not only in the MUP and the TO." That's at number 4. At number 5: "Police, they have formed a Krajina police. It must start functioning vertically and horizontally." Number 6, and I'm missing things out obviously, but I'm just trying to move swiftly: "Select the best people for the police." And then at the bottom: "The JNA will supplement admission to the police. The JNA will give three to five --" we're going over the page to B/C/S page 42 and English 42. "The JNA will give three to five people for the Krajina MUP, give blue clothing to the MUP from the RV but not more than 6.000 sets. They are asking for tanks, armoured personnel carriers, and helicopters. They can only get armoured combat vehicles which should be repainted."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, it was a slip of the tongue when you refer to Babic, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If I did, certainly it was a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is this your understanding of the situation as it's described: the JNA were expected to give some commanding officers to the Krajina MUP, and not only that, they're expected to give, at least according to Martic and at least according to the JNA, certain supplies - weapons, ammunition, and so on?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's my understanding of the situation, precisely as we read it here. But let me just add. This is no longer the JNA. They had withdrawn. There were only officers who hailed from Krajina. On the 22nd of April, the JNA was already gone. In February, they were still insisting, though already preparing for departure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to page 46 of the English and page 46 of B/C/S. And we're staying with the same date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And Babic -- I do it again. Mladic writes: "The JNA will not pay the police --" this is halfway down the page in English. "The JNA will not pay the police but only our officers active in the MUP and the TO." Now, was that -- from what you've said a few moments ago, that was your understanding, at least in part, that the police would not be financed by the JNA directly. Was it also your understanding that the JNA would finance, though, the officers that it gave - and I say the JNA, but the -- what remained of the army - would -- from Belgrade, would finance the officers who had been placed in commanding roles within the MUP and the TO as well?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was aware of it at the time. It wasn't even considered a secret. That's to say that the officers would continue receiving salaries from their commands. At least initially, because nobody regarded the Vance Plan as something that was going to be happening short-term only [as interpreted], and they didn't know what was going to happen then if things went on for a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you aware that Martic was making such -- well, on one view, grandiose requests for his police force; requests for helicopters, for example?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I didn't know. This is the first time I'm seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's have, please, if we can, on the screen 1D02586.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what I'm going to show you are stenographic records from the 187th Session of the Presidency of the SFRY held on the 20th of February, 1992, so around the same time as Mladic's entries, beginning at --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 1 so we can see who's present. And just for the record: So we can see that the likes of Petar Gracanin, the federal secretary of the interior, is there; Adzic, acting federal secretary of national defence. Neither of the two accused are present. And if we go to page 45 of the English, please, and page 82 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And we can see there the section is dealing with "the report on direct preparations for and activities relating to the admission of UN peacekeeping forces?" And just going down to the page to Adzic and his comments. And I'm going to move swiftly through this to save time. Adzic notes that he'd received Martic within 45 minutes. "It seems to me that some things have been misunderstood. He's going for a police force of 20.000 men. No European country has so many policemen. He has asked me for helicopters and 150 all-terrain vehicles. I would have to empty a whole army group, including its soldiers, and give it to him." Then over the page, to page 46 of the English: [As read] "But let me make myself clear: I'll give everything I can give. But we should see tomorrow, and the federal SUP and the MUP of Serbia should be here to see how many policemen should be there, because Krajina cannot be defended by those policemen. There are other ways." One line down: [As read] "I have prepared some airmen's uniforms for them to wear. Serbia probably has to be give something. Some money has to be allocated for making purchases. Weapons - what is available, what is needed - we will give what we can; but I certainly cannot --" sorry, "I certainly can't give them helicopters for the police. Tanks won't be recognised - that won't be given them either -- that won't be given either," et cetera. Are you able to confirm that it was Adzic who was principally the contact who was expected to provide the Krajina police, post-Vance, with what they required: Weapons, ammunition, logistics, and the like, uniforms, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I'm reading these notes - this is the first time I see it - it seems that all these things were supposed to come from the JNA. Under the Vance Plan, the RSK was not entitled to an army, and that's why Martic was asking for 20.000 men. There was still a threat present at the outlying boundaries of the territory, and we didn't have any armed men.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you able to testify to any conversations you had with Martic or any conversations you were told about where Martic was insisting that the police would effectively be the army and that's why he saw it as his duty to approach the likes of Adzic for supplies?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did discuss this topic before the State Security Service was dissolved. Some sort of a peace plan was expected. We didn't know the details. Though Martic was informed - probably somebody from the top Serbian leadership did tell him - that peace forces would be sent from the UN and that the RSK with not be entitled to an army. He knew that he had to sign a peace plan but -- and also that he had to have some sort of a force that would, first of all, maintain law and order, and, second of all, should there come an attack from Croatia, there should be a contingent of armed men, even if they only carried side-arms. I didn't see him for a while after that meeting, so I don't know what his response was in relation to the peace plan and its application.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if we go to page 47 of the English and 86 of the B/C/S, please. We'll see Adzic continuing to speak at this Presidency session. Where he notes -- and I'm interested in the paragraph that begins: "That's what I wanted to let you know." And we can see that Adzic continues to complain about Martic's rather large and ambitious requests. And then he notes: "I believe that once we have resolved this we will request consent from the Presidency for this equipment and these things to be given to the Republic of Serbian Krajina." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that this was the chain of authority, effectively, for the supplies coming from Belgrade to the Krajina: Martic to Adzic, Adzic to the Presidency, Presidency make a decision, supplies come to the RSK?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if we go to page 49 of the English and 89 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We'll see a speech by Gracanin, who, I think it's agreed, was the federal secretary of the interior, who's noting in response to a discussion about the Territorial Defence of the RSK refusing to give up their weapons: "All right, we should now look into that," he said. "This is very hard. It's not easy to separate one's self from one's weapon. We should understand them in that respect. But if we have good organisation, those handing over their weapons will certainly find it easier to do so once they have seen that the police are well organised. If this meeting is held tomorrow, we must start working as soon as possible along three or four different lines. As for the financial part with regard to the police, some loans have been taken out." Are you able to testify to what Gracanin said there and the role that Gracanin played in relation to ensuring adequate finances for the RSK MUP?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically about the financing and whether the RSK government took loans in order to pay out salaries and finance itself, I really don't know that. I'm seeing this for the first time. If there were such borrowings, then that's probably that, and it went to the Krajina government which then probably made the transfer of funds for the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to D56, please, another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This document, as you'll see, comes from -- well, I'll wait until it comes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, could we ask one. And we are talking about financing, what is discussed on the 20th of February. Was there any financing foreseen by Belgrade, by Yugoslavia, for reservists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was still the period when the Yugoslav People's Army existed. All the officer salaries and all the active and reserve units went through the Main Staff or the Ministry of Defence or, as it was called at the time, the Federal Secretariat for National Defence in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for reservists, did that continue after the JNA was withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the withdrawal of the JNA and the organising of the Serbian Army of the Krajina, I think that stopped. I don't know if the defence ministry of the Krajina received loans from the Ministry of Defence of Serbia. It's something that I don't know. But I think that in the beginning the budget of the Krajina government was composed of loans and other donations, because the economy there was not very developed. So I guess that the money was obtained in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say it was loans from the federal government rather than other payments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat: I am not able to say that exactly, if I might put it that way. I was low ranking at the time, so I couldn't really know how the government obtained or borrowed money. Here I see that there were some loans, so I assume that the government did borrow money in order to be able to finance its budget. But I don't know from whom and how it borrowed the money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also do not know whether it was limited to loans or whether there were any direct payments in support of the budget. Not being loans.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know if there were any direct payments or how the payments were made or how things were paid out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps I can hopefully assist a little with that. Could we go to - could we stay with the same document, please - page 47 of the English, and B/C/S page 84. I don't know if this is what Your Honour had in mind, but I hope it might assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to, so I don't know whether it coincides with what I had on my mind. But let's -- ask your questions and I may find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What we're going to see now again is a continuation of the Adzic speech which we've been discussing. And at the top of the English page, Adzic says: "Martic has made another request, which is not unfounded. Today, between 30.000 and 40.000 reservists from the Krajinas are receiving some sort of food allowance. He says if we discontinue it immediately there will be widespread famine, which is not far from the absolute truth; because that's what people live off there. It's this base money issue. He ... asked that this be extended by at least two or three months, which I don't think should be a big problem; we should do this at the coast of all this - the system should start functioning. And he is asking intelligent questions even though he's not a businessman. Businessmen should go there quickly to establish something, to create something that could support Krajina, because Serbia and the mint certainly won't be able to withstand that." Do you know anything about that, Mr. Draca? When I say "about that," about the supply of food in substitute for wages, with the expectation that reservists would, several months after the implementation of the Vance Plan, then be supported by local businesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may be my lack of knowledge of the English language, but food and food allowance is not the same to me. Food allowance could be in terms of money; whereas, food supplies is that you provide bread or ... "The supply of food in substitute for wages," you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour is absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know anything about -- then about payments made to reservists and perhaps to be continued in order to allow them to buy food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All mobilised reservists in the JNA received their salary by way of daily remuneration. Whoever had their job and was mobilised would receive a part of his salary in the company where he was employed, and the rest he would receive from the JNA per day of service. Martic was probably concerned because the economy was in a shambles because of the war, that because they did not receive proper compensation, they would not have enough means to support themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the question more specifically was whether you know anything about reservists receiving food allowance which, as is proposed here, which would then continue. And, I take it, to continue even after they were not JNA reservists anymore. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is exactly what I was saying. There was no particular compensation for food. But from what I understand of what is written here, what he wanted to say was that the money that they were receiving was enough just for food for them to survive. As far as I know, there was no special compensation for food, but there were per diem payments which were paid out on a monthly basis, but this was very low. It was just enough for food, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question focusses on these kind of payments to be continued even after they had quitted their positions as JNA reservists and financed from, if I could say it briefly, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whoever remained in the police units would continue to receive their salary, but no longer as per diems but as a salary from the Ministry of Interior. The financing of the ministry and the government is something that I really cannot talk about. I don't know where they got their funds from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if the number of 30- to 40.000 reservists is mentioned, they did not remain in the police force, did they? Reservists of the JNA by that number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they did not. This is the number that the JNA mobilised by 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have D56 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, Madam Registrar reminds me that there was an issue about the provenance of D56, a document which had been tendered earlier but was not admitted and was then re-tendered by the Simatovic Defence, but which is, as far as I understand, not in evidence at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's right. It was not admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is there any news about the provenance or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the part that we indicated provenance before, and we can't really take it any further than that, what I was hoping to do was ask the witness about the contents and see if he can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. To see whether he can --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- we can get there by different routes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then the status of the document is clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. D56.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If you have a look at this document coming on the screen and see if can you assist with its contents. If I can summarize what the document appears to be and see if you can comment on this. It appears to be a document sent by Gracanin to Sokolovic of the Serbian MUP explaining the decision of the Presidency which had been dealing with organising or certainly laying out some kind of plan for the organisation of the internal affairs service in the RSK. Do you know anything about this subject? Are you able to confirm any of the contents of the document?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm seeing this document for the first time. In view of the fact that in that period I was not working at the Ministry of the Interior in Knin, I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Let's move on, then. To save time, I will not refer you to a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: P1226 [Realtime transcript read in error "1266"], Your Honours, is -- deals with the financing of the -- sorry, the supplies to the MUP units of the RSK in February of 1992. Could we have on the screen, please, P2445.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, as we can see, this is a federal Secretariat of the Interior document dated the 12th of March, 1992, and it's being sent to the Ministry of Interior of the Serbian DB. And the section I'm particularly interested in, it's an Official Note, as we can see, if we go to the second page, concerning a talk that's been had with Martic on the 9th of March, a talk between Chief Inspector Djurovic and Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 3 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I want to see if you're able to cast some further light on this issue. So 12th of March, 1992. The report -- and the report notes: "Martic particularly stressed that they no longer had ... reservations with regard to the composition of the SUP staff and that they were fully prepared to accept any form of co-operation with the SUP." Which, I suggest, reads as if prior to this Martic not only had a problem with the Serbian DB, but he had a problem with the federal Secretariat of the SUP and had not been co-operating with them prior to this date. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. He wasn't co-operating. And as it states here, he had some reserves towards the cadre and the leadership of the federal SUP. But I don't know what the reasons were for Martic's thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Does that mean - and I'm not asking you to speculate. If you know, you know; if you don't, you don't - does that mean that -- was that an explanation concerning why Martic and the RSK MUP replied upon donations for a period of time in 1991 and 1992, because they weren't getting any help from the federal SUP and they weren't getting any help from the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, this is a period when there was no help from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, again, I'm not asking you to speculate, but from this time onwards is it -- is it your understanding that Martic then began to look to the army in Belgrade and then, at times, to the federal SUP for assistance? Professional assistance such as expertise.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, may I seek clarification. You document you have not used, P1266, where you said was about -- let me see what you said exactly. Which deals with -- you said the supplies to the MUP units of the RSK in February of 1992. As far as I'm aware, P1266 is an instruction to Republika Srpska and Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina to send reports by 8.00 this evening, not specifically focussing on any supplies to the MUP units. So therefore I'm puzzled by -- even if you did not deal with it with the witness, apparently there is some --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I misspoke, and I apologise. I seem to be doing it a lot this morning. It's P1226.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1226. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1406 will receive number D679, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I don't want to re-start the discussion, but the mere fact that documents are on a web site, as may be known to many of us, does not necessarily mean that it is a public document. I think WikiLeaks has shown that not everything what is found on the web is by its nature meant to be public. So if you would please carefully look at it again, to the sources. And, Mr. Farr, if you would nevertheless try to find out. The document is provisionally put under seal, up to the moment where we -- you have verified what web site you consulted, Mr. Jordash. And, Mr. Farr, you will have an opportunity to further verify as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have 1D02090, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, 1D02090.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is a document, Mr. Draca, which I think you've seen, because it was part of the documents we gave you a couple of days ago. So we ought to move -- be able to move fairly swiftly. Do you recall the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the time these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: At the time these documents were provided to the witness, we indicated that given that the witness was going to have a chance to review them before coming to court, that's it's the Prosecution's position that an independent foundation for knowledge regarding the contents of the document should be established before the document is used so we'll know what the witness is testifying to from personal knowledge and what he may have learned by reviewing the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, would you keep this in back of your mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, this is a document -- I will, Your Honour, but this is a document which relates to the issue we've been discussing for the last 45 minutes, and I think the witness has laid a very serious foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could be, but I do not know what questions you're going to put to the witness, so it's difficult for me to -- to say yes or no to Mr. Farr. That's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's have a look at the first page just very quickly with reference to a meeting between the SSNO and various representatives from the RSK concerning the replenishment of materiel and technical equipment for the TO units and staffs as well as the police organs and units of the RSK. And then going over to page 2: "It was concluded," the document notes, and I quote, "that the police organs and units will be given 20.000 outfits, and a hundred all-terrain vehicles. Regarding other equipment, the MUP was tasked to submit requests on replenishments." When you rejoined the RSK DB, was this the situation that you found, i.e., that requests were being made by -- the RSK MUP on a regular basis to the SSNO?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know of the period after I rejoined the Ministry of the Interior, the MUP did not send requests directly to the SSNO. Rather, they went through the RSK government.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And then the RSK government went to the SSNO. That was the chain of requests for supplies.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I tendered the document, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It would have assisted me, at least, Mr. Jordash if at the beginning the dates of the document would have been clear to me, but I see now that on the first page it's the 7th of April, 1992 .

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D2090 will receive number D680, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D680 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have 1D02096, please. This is one of several documents which deal with federal secretary and delivering -- and delivery of arms for the reserves and MUP divisions of the RSK. And you've read this document; am I correct? Would you agree that this is consistent with your understanding of how things worked at the time? That's April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And let's go to 1D01370.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is a similar document, dated the 25th of April, 1992. And it's significant, perhaps, insofar as it details supplies but also refers to - halfway down the page or a third of the way down the page: "A Federal Secretariat for National Defence resolution, top secret, number 352-1, dated the 20th of April, 1992." Were you aware of that resolution and it, as described in the document, being designed to fulfil the ammunition requests of the MUP of RSK?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know of this specific document at the time, but I knew that things like that did occur in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I tender the last two documents, but may I also tender from the bar table, with agreement from the Prosecution, similar documents: First of all, 1D02026, relating to the Okucani MUP station; 1D02027, relating to the Knin MUP station; 1D02028, relating to the Petrinja MUP station; 1D02072, relating to the MUP station of Benkovac. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first document was 1D2090; this will receive number D681, Your Honours. Then document 1D1370 will receive number D682, Your Honours. Then the next one was 1D2026, will receive number D683. And it seems that I cannot find -- next ones are not picked up in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- will receive number D684, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- will receive number D685, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- will receive number D686, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the transcript doesn't -- as it now stands, doesn't reflect exactly what Mr. Jordash said, just to put that on the record so there's no confusion regarding which documents have which numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that special attention will be paid when reviewing the transcript on the numbers. D681 up to and including D686 are admitted into evidence. Mr. Jordash, you say it's all about distribution of equipment, arms, et cetera. Now, just for my understanding, I think one of the first document or the second was about fire-arms, and we are talking about ten, I think, or 20 -- it's very limited number. Whereas the document now, with the ammunition, is well over a million pieces of ammunition. Is there any further guidance for us to see how the one relates to the other? Of course it could be that there are 200 similar documents with ten weapons. That makes 20.000. And then 20.000 to a million is easier -- is an easier jump than ten rifles or -- I can't get them all on my screen immediately, but I'm thinking in terms of quantities, whether the ammunition matches the number of weapons provided to, if I understand you well, the MUP of Republic of Serbian Krajina. You understand what I -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One rifle and 10 million cartridges, I have some difficulties, and, of course, I'm now exaggerating, but I'm trying to -- to look at the matters in the context, not having looked at the documents themselves in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly from the documents that we have, and have seen, you are not able to correlate between weapons and ammunition. All these are, are effectively lists of ammunition provided, with very little indication of the -- the -- the weapons and the amount of weapons delivered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- or possessed by the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm saying this because if I would have one rifle and if I would receive a million cartridges, I would consider to share some of it with my neighbours. That's ... therefore, I'm trying to look at the quantitative aspects as well. But if you say there's -- it's difficult to -- to clearly make a link between numbers in this respect, then that is accepted and the puzzle remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, the amount of ammunition is noteworthy, because it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I did --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- it is large.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Especially -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, you know, if you have no explanation to provide with this witness, then we move on, and the puzzle is -- remains. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm about to move to Pauk. I don't know if this is a good time for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's the right time for a break. Could you give us an indication, Mr. Jordash, on how much time you'd need after the break. I think your initial estimate was two hours, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. I think I would like 45 minutes, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 45 minutes. I think that fits well into the original estimate. You have 45 minutes after the break. And we'll resume at a quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you may proceed. I'm looking at the clock. It's ten minutes to 11.00 now. 45 minutes for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have P1289.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to deal with the subject of Pauk, Mr. Draca. From what you've told us, you met and discussed at length the issue of Pauk with Fikret Abdic. I want to ask you about a particular view that he may have expressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: P -- P1289, a report from the Republic of Serbian Krajina army. If we go to page 4 of the English, please, and I'm hoping, although I don't have an indication, that's it's page 4 of B/C/S. It's the title the "National Defence of the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia Forces." And the document is dated 20th of November, 1994. And it appears to be some sort of security assessment. And the section I'm interested in is the sentence beginning: "A very admiral initiative of F. Abdic to proclaim this area a protected area or to make this area a UN protectorate ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise for interrupting. But it seems that my learned friend misspoke when stating the date of the document, and I'm raising this merely to avoid misleading the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The record says 20th of November, 1994, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You're right. And it was -- the document has a stamp which shows it was received on that, it seems, by the Republic of Serbian Krajina government, but in fact the date of the document, the operative time on the front page is stated as 2000 hours on 18th of August, 1994. Thank you to Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And have you found the section, Mr. Draca, dealing with the very admirably initiative of Abdic to proclaim this area a protected area or make this area an UN protectorate with the help from UNPROFOR was not accepted? Fikret Abdic has accepted negotiations on the local level in order to organise the Defence and gain some time.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to also ask you to look at another document before I ask you a question. 1D05296, which is a letter from Abdic to the then-UN Secretary General Boutros-Ghali, which unfortunately hasn't scanned, it seems, very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We do have a paper copy. Perhaps it would be easier for the witness if we gave him the paper copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If you just have a skim through this letter, which is a -- as I've said, a letter from Abdic to Ghali, and it's dated 7th of October, 1994. Have you had an opportunity to have skim a through it?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've read it careful the day before yesterday when you gave me the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, my apologies. Was this a view that Fikret Abdic was expressing on a regular basis, a view that he was desperate for the UN to come in or the international community to provide assistance to his people in the Bihac region?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The only difference between this and the previous document lies in the fact that the previous document was written several days before they fled to the RSK territory, whereas this document was produced in such a way that Fikret Abdic complained directly to the UN general -- Secretary-General of the conduct exhibited by the UN forces already at the point after they had fled. A member of the UN Polish Battalion opened fire on the refugees who were attempting to enter the territory of the Republic of Croatia illegally. Everything else, however, is correct, where he describes the sentiments of the people, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I tender the Fikret Abdic letter, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we haven't received any information on the provenance of this document, so we have an objection to authenticity, pending that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I MFI it and we'll provide the information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D5296 will receive number D687, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the reality is as you saw it - is this right? - and the reality is as Fikret Abdic saw it, that absent any action by the international community, absent any action by the UN, the only protection for his people from the 5th Corps was to seek help from Serbia and to seek help from the RSK? Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And so that we're clear: Help from an army, the 5th Corps, which was, even by the standards of this Balkans crisis, an extremely vicious army when it came to treatment of civilians?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It was well known, especially the 505th Brigade, was known of their -- for their cruelty towards civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And, in fact, one of the problems that Fikret Abdic had was that his own army was actually too frightened, in many respects, to even face the 5th Corps because of that reputation. Is that something that Fikret Abdic talked about?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. Fikret Abdic did talk about that. But we also had intelligence information from several sources confirming this to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, P1285. It's a document which is a security organ of the Main Staff of the Serbian Army of Krajina, dated the 30th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I want to go, please, first of all, to the first page so you can just orientate yourself as to the nature of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And then if we can go to page 2 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this is a document which ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If you just have a quick look at that. This is a document which is entitled "Explanation, Situation in the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia." And on page 2 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S we have reference to three meetings, the VRSK and the VJ representatives held three meetings with APZB president Fikret Abdic in Lika Kladusa with the aim of preparing an offensive activity by the APZB forces to regain seized territory and liberate new territories ending at the Zezin [phoen] area. Now, if you go further down the page, you see meetings referred to with Celeketic and Mladic and Perisic and also Stanisic. And then further down the page you see the sentence: "According to Abdic, president of the RSK government Borislav Mikelic was to realize the delivery of weapons and ammunition to the APZB." Was that consistent with your understanding in the middle of 1994, that the assistance that was being proposed at that stage was assistance which would, in terms of weapons and ammunition, come from the RSK to Pauk? That was the channel of weapons and ammunition proposed to assist Abdic. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Probably you perhaps made an error. Pauk was not established in that period. This is June 1994, when Fikret Abdic and the majority of the people are still in Kladusa. They're still in their territory, but they had lost a part of the territory that they were staying in up until that time. Already at that time, if I can put it that way, there was panic beginning to spread among the population. They didn't know what to do. And so I think this document, as I understand it, is Abdic's attempt to return the territory and was asking for help from the VRSK and the Army of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you're absolute right; I misspoke. Let me just clarify this. The period before Pauk began in late 1994, around November, the period before that, this -- the, if we can say, the operations which were perhaps a precursor to Pauk, the weapons and ammunition were coming from the RSK to Fikret Abdic. Is that fair enough?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, if we go to -- if we can have, please, 65 ter 5609, ERN 0668-2082-B/C/S-ET. And the e-court page 114 B/C/S and 115 English. This is a Mladic notebook. And the entry is dated 13th of October, 1994, and it's a meeting with commanders of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps, 15 Corps, 21st Corps, and 39 Corps. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, but I don't see the corps that you mentioned. It just states "the commander of the 11th Brigade" here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... You're right. We don't have the right Mladic excerpt on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It should be one relating to the 13th of October, and it should be 65 ter 5609. And it should be page 114 of the B/C/S and 115 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Whilst that's coming up, we're going to look at a meeting involving the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps and the 15th Corps and the 21st Corps and the 39th Corps. These were all units of which army, Mr. Draca?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry. They were the units of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can see, yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this entry dated the 13th of October, 1994, if we go over the page to something that Mladic records General Celeketic saying. Page 115 of the B/C/S and 116 of the English. And Celeketic notes: "We are the Serbian army, one army. Nobody has betrayed you, it was just the way it was. Our MTS situation is worse than yours. We have problems with ammunition. I received the task that we should do as much as we can. Since the Serbian MUP is not coming and since they are not sending the MTS, I will light the fire by the 15th Corps and the 39th Corps and help towards Kladusa." Are you able to comment on this discussion? Am I correct that Celeketic was supposed to be providing supplies; was not providing sufficient supplies, according to Fikret Abdic; no supplies were coming from the Serbian MUP in October of 1994 and prior to that?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So we're clear: How did you -- how do you know that? What's your source of knowledge for that?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the chief of the state security department, I was also a member of the Supreme Defence Council of the RSK, and Celeketic did report back about this matter at a meeting. Actually, at several meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But was -- am I correct that the problem wasn't weapons, because Fikret Abdic had many weapons, in part because the VRS left their weapons to him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The problem was in the ammunition and in artillery shells, of which there was a shortage in the Krajina. And you can see from this text that Celeketic, as the chief of the General Staff of the RSK army, was complaining to Mladic about the things that we were just commenting on just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did -- did -- did this -- did that situation then change as a result of Abdic's complaint to Celeketic, and Celeketic's complaint to Mladic?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing changed in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did there come a time when it did change during the currency of the Pauk operation?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later, when the operation to return began, the return of the units of the Army of western Bosnia, the Main Staff of the RSK army secured a number of ammunition pieces for the use of Fikret Abdic. But I don't know where that was obtained from, whether it was from the existing VRSK reserves or if they received assistance from Republika Srpska or the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you don't know that? I'm not suggesting you should, but is there any reason why you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army has its own chains of command, and this is not some major thing that they would need to report to anybody from the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I want to now just widen the discussion a little bit to the assistance provided by the RSK to the Pauk operation and Bihac in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I have on the screen, please, 1D05297.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is a map that we, in the Defence, have drawn. And I want to ask you if this corresponds to your knowledge concerning the locations of the military formations of the 11th Corps in 1994 and 1995 within Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that this is a map of Eastern Slavonia and Baranja, but I cannot remember. I don't know if I ever knew specifically where all the forces were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't know if the Prosecution dispute this or not, but are you able to give any indication of whether this was your general understanding of the spread of the 11th Corps military formations? Were these the approximate area that they were based in, in 1994 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that that was so. Can I see the deployment. There was concentration along the roads, along the river Drava. Yes, I think that that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know anything about Mirkovci, as can you see on the map; was there military formations there?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. Because that place bordered with the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There's been a suggestion in this case that the only military formation in Mirkovci was the Boca's unit, the Skorpions. Do you agree that that's not true?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. The Skorpions were a paramilitary unit in our mind that was not part of the 11th Corps in Knin. At least as far as we knew. And it was used to secure the Opatovci oil facilities, and it was engaged by the NIK, the oil industry of the Krajina. And I know --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I interrupted you. You know ...

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, during that period that was that -- the task that they were executing, the security for the oil facilities, in order to avoid -- well, how can I put it so that you understand me? They did not belong to the 11th Corps, but so that we would not treat them as a paramilitary unit, they had signed a contract with the oil industry and they were providing security for the oil installations at Opatovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just to be clear: They were not based at Mirkovci; they were in Djeletovci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Djeletovci and Opatovci are close by and they were in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Erdut at this time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, could I ask. Could you then tell us which unit of the 11th Corps was in Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly. Some brigade or some battalion that was part of the 11th Corps. But I don't know the names of the units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not knowing the names, what's the basis of your knowledge on who were in Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Other than the armed forces of the VRSK and the police, which already in 1994, especially in Slavonia and Baranja where peace had been established for a while, the police was carrying out regular police work. No one could have been in that area other than units of the 11th Corps. I don't know exactly how they were deployed. I really cannot remember that. Perhaps I didn't ever know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you -- if you say - and let me quote you then literally - "No one could have been in that area other than units of the 11th Corps." Now, one of the previous questions of Mr. Jordash was: "They were in Djeletovci," when he was referring to the -- when he was referring to the Skorpions. That's the same region, isn't it? It's a distance of only a few kilometres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's close by. But Mirkovci was specific because it was the most forward point towards Vinkovci. It was where the first strike was supposed to hit --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last portion of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The specific thing about Mirkovci: Its strategic position meant that it was very important for the RSK defence, because it was located in such a place that a possible attack by the Republic of Croatia would be conducted along one of the axes leading to Mirkovci, and that's why Mirkovci was a very fortified location. As for the other villages, Djeletovci, Opatovci, that seems to be very close on the map. They seem very close by. But actually, as far as the defence is concerned, they were not like Mirkovci or had nothing in common with Mirkovci in that sense at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you described to us the tasks of the Skorpions. Now, do you know whether they were in Djeletovci, yes or no? Was that compatible with the task they were given? Or don't you just know? I'd like to ... if you know, tell us what the basis of your knowledge is. If you say, "Well, I really don't know; I know what their task was, but apart from that, I do not know whether they were in Djeletovci," please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as their assignment is concerned, it's exactly as I said what it was before. They were providing security for the facilities of the oil industry. The place where they were billeted, however, as far as I recall, was in Djeletovci, which was in the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what's the basis for this recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The State Security Service of the Krajina was observing, or monitoring, this unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have on the screen, please, 1D02572.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to ask you about Erdut. Am I correct that at this time, the time we're talking about, Erdut -- there was in Erdut the Ministry of Defence; that's where it was stationed?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, this may be my problem rather than anyone else's, but I'm not entirely clear exactly what time we're talking about at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly 1994 and 1995, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Am I correct that the Ministry of Defence was stationed in Erdut in 1994 and 1995? If you can be more specific than me and help Mr. Farr, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The defence ministry seat was in Knin. One of the ministry's buildings was in Erdut, where the deputy minister was staying. Slavonia and Baranja are physically separated from the rest of the Krajina, and all the deputies were located in the ministries, and I think each of the ministries - I'm not sure whether it was each single one - also had offices in the area of Slavonia and Baranja.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If you look at the document on the screen dated 21st of June --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, everything that the witness said about who is in the offices in the area of Slavonia and Baranja was not recorded in the transcript, so perhaps it would be a good idea to ask the witness to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat who were in the offices, the offices of the ministries in Slavonia and Baranja.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically in the building that Mr. Jordash asked about was where the deputy minister was located. But other ministries also in that area, perhaps not in Erdut but in Beli Manastir and Vukovar, were also represented in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, unfortunately again it's not stated which deputy of the defence minister was located. The witness said it, but it's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, your guidance was not very precise in that respect. Apparently you have told us which deputy minister of defence was in the Slavonia and Baranja branch office, if I could say so. Could you give us his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not recall the name right now, but it was Janovic [as interpreted], aka, Mrgud. We already referred to him before. Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. 21st of June, 1995, an RDB's report. Could we go, please, to page 5 of the English and page 5 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm interested in what it describes as being based in Erdut as well: "Apart from the army, in the event of Croatia's aggression, the detachment of the PJM of the SUP of Beli Manastir would also be included in the defence and would be attached to the 60th Brigade for anti-landing and anti-sabotage activities. According to establishment, the detachment is part of the brigade and is based in Erdut; it is made up of active-duty and reserve ... officers." Are you able to confirm that this was a unit of armed men in Erdut in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't manage to find that paragraph. I would like to read it before I give my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's -- let me find precisely where that is, but we'll come back to that. In the meantime, I want to ask you about a related topic, which is this: Am I correct that before Pauk and during Pauk battalions from the 11th Corps were being sent on a monthly basis to assist Abdic?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What about during Pauk? Isn't it correct that battalions from the 11th Corps were being sent during Pauk?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "battalion" is exaggerated. These may have been individual groups of officers. I don't know of a single battalion having come to the aid during Pauk.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Smaller military units then. Are you aware of military units being sent? Let's stick with that. If you're not, you're not. I mean, I don't want to detain you if you don't know something.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm going to return to a subject, but it looks, because you don't know this subject, as though I'm actually going to finish on time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I take instructions, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll give you an opportunity to add something after we've heard from Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If I can ask a few more questions, not many, I think I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps we first give an opportunity to the witness to add something to, I take it, one of your previous answers. Please add whatever you'd like to add.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As discussed yesterday, Milorad Ulemek, Legija, came along with a group to Pauk. He had been at the centre in Erdut. The Skorpions, too, appeared for the Pauk operation, but for a couple of days only, before they returned to Slavonia. If these are the units you meant, then I can confirm that. But there were no battalions coming from the 11th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think we'll have to disagree on that, Mr. Draca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no reason to express agreement or disagreement --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with the witness, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain what the role of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I see that we were "[Overlapping speakers] ..." Not saying who overlapped who, but I'd like to have this clearly on the record: I said there's no reason to express agreement or disagreement with the witness, and apparently you agreed. And I invited you to put your next question to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You say there were no battalions coming from the 11th Corps, and you've told us that the group led by Ulemek and also the Skorpions did go to Pauk. Were they sent by the 11th Corps?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. At the proposal of Deputy Defence Minister Milanovic, that I've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were any smaller units sent, do you know, by the 11th Corps at any point to assist in the Bihac operations?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about it, truly. There may have been, without my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know the role of the 21st, the 17th, and the 39th Corps in the Bihac operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask which period you're referring to? Because there were several operations around Bihac in the span of four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's stay with, first of all, with pre-Pauk 1994. Do you know if those corps had a role to play in the operations to assist Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their role was to tie up forces of the 5th Corps towards Bihac so that they may not have extensive forces in the direction of Kladusa to mount resistance to Abdic's forces. Now, which elements of the corps were sent to the Bihac region or which units were sent from within that corps, I truly don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know whether they continued to have a role in Pauk? And if so, what was the role?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Until the end of the operation, they engaged in combat in the direction of Bihac. That was their basic role. Perhaps it would be important to say that the military and state leadership of the RSK was of the view that they should not enter that territory, but engage in combat along the boundaries merely to tie up the forces of the corps. The same thing was agreed with the VRS, who did the same thing at their end of that region.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the VRS did it with their special brigade of the MUP Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part with them too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now I want to just ask you about two documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If Your Honours allow.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are the last ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have, please, on the screen 1D05293. English page 48, B/C/S 46, ERN 0-- sorry, B/C/S 47. ERN 0415-1185.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And these are intercepts, or summaries of intercepted conversations. And I want to ask you about two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: English page 48 and B/C/S 47. ERN 0415-1185.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's 25th of August, 1995: "Today at 4.00 p.m. in Ilok the commander of the 11th Corps, General Dusan Loncar, will meet the General Bora Ivanovic, the co-ordinator between Yugoslavia army and the 11th Corps of SVK. The topic of the meeting is not known." Are you able to confirm that that was the role of Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately I can't confirm that because I don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Let's go to one more.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Document -- same 65 ter, English page 49, B/C/S 48, ERN 0415-1258.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This intercept relates to the document which we started to look at, and it notes from discussions of Obrad Stevanovic (MUP Serbia) who is in command of the 11th Corps, we learn that two divisions of active police officers (special police officers) have been sent from Serbia to occupied territory today on the 21st of October, 1995." Do you know anything about that, or Obrad Stevanovic's role?

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know much about it. By that time Knin had fallen and the RSK was destroyed. I was no longer involved in that job. So I wasn't in a position to be privy to details surrounding these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jordash, it's only a couple of minutes ago that I said there would be no need to express disagreement with the witness. Unless, of course - and that's not what I thought you were doing, but I might be wrong - that you were eliciting evidence in support of your own case and that you were about - apart from disagreeing with the witness - to put to the witness what your case is so as to give him an opportunity to explain himself. I didn't gain that impression for two reasons: First, because the witness spontaneously asked to add something, so it was not specifically perhaps on a question you put to him. And the second is that I gained the impression that you just wanted to say, "We disagree," without that being a first step to put to the witness what your case was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, and we first -- I don't know if it's worth me saying what our case is on that, or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I know that you're very precise on the Rule 90(H)(ii), so therefore I wanted -- when I stopped you at that moment, I don't know whether this is such a detail of your case or I don't know whether you seek to -- the witness to further explain. It might be fair to the witness. That's the only thing I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the witness has said that smaller units may have been sent, he just doesn't know. And it's our case that smaller units or units of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please address the witness if you ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, just so you know, Mr. Witness, that we suggest that units were being sent from the 11th Corps on a fairly regular basis. Now, whether they were the size of a battalion or smaller, we've not been able to ascertain that, but we're saying that certain -- certainly units other than Skorpions and other than Ulemek's Group were sent on a regular basis. You understand our position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does this trigger any addition to the answer you gave earlier? If not, we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If I can add, just briefly, that the size of a battalion is over 500 men. And perhaps that's the point which added to the confusion. It is quite possible that smaller units did come, but I wasn't aware of it. And besides, I added that I wasn't a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I ask one further question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just this:

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You and I have never met, have we? Or you've never met anyone from the Stanisic Defence team.

utterances.speaker: ACO DRACA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, are you ready? I would have one question to the witness. And I sometimes put them to the witness in order not to lose the context in which the previous questions were asked. Mr. Draca, Mr. Jordash took you to document P1289, which describes the whole situation with the 5th Corps and Bihac and the admirable initiative to -- to -- to put it under protection. You remember that document and the issues discussed in that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was the document which was shown to you prior to the letter by Mr. Abdic to -- to New York. That's -- it's clear. Now, was there any role for Mr. Stanisic to be played in that ongoing -- these ongoing events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me say that the top leadership of the Republic of Serbia, yes. That was our estimate. We saw Serbia as the guarantor of the agreement signed between the Republic of the Serbian Krajina and Republika Srpska. When we look at the problem more generally and in relation to the international community, the RSK leadership, having no other contacts, was gravitating toward President Milosevic. The Republic of Serbia at the time was a recognised country. It had its diplomacy. And all of the factors were conducive toward Belgrade. Now, to what extent there were reactions from Belgrade and from whom, that's something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said: "... having no other contacts, was gravitating toward President Milosevic." My question is: Was there any -- I do understand that President Milosevic, being the head of the government, was interested -- was there any specific involvement of Mr. Stanisic? So, next to President Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're discussing the period up until Operation Pauk and during that operation. I don't know if Mr. Stanisic was involved, save for the fact that we sent reports to the top echelons of state security on refugees, et cetera, because we could not approach Milosevic. So we did inform the State Security Service of both Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbia on the situation in Kladusa. Now, as to whether Mr. Stanisic received any tasks relating to these issues from President Milosevic, that's something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
